0.long_answer: Albinism in plants is largely due to a deficiency of the pigment molecules that are associated with the photosystems. In normal plant cells, chlorophyll molecules are organized in and around both Photosystem I and Photosystem II where they play a central role in capturing light energy for photosynthesis. When there is insufficient chlorophyll—whether because of genetic mutations affecting the biosynthetic enzymes or other disruptions—the photosynthetic apparatus cannot properly assemble or function. This leads to a loss of green coloration in the leaves, resulting in the albino phenotype.
